title: Easton follows great loss with victory
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton follows great loss with victory

 April 6, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1245
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton High assistant baseball coach Matt Blue died Friday night after a 17-month battle with cancer.Less than 24 hours later, the Warriors were back on the field, having decided to go forward with Saturday's home game against Southern-Anne Arundel.
And Blue's son Dustin wanted the ball.
"He wanted to pitch," Easton head coach Albert Pritchett said of his sophomore right-hander. "We talked before the game. He wanted to pitch."
Dustin Blue pitched three-plus innings of two-hit ball before running into a jam in the fourth inning, but by then the Warriors had built a lead that was never in jeopardy en route to an emotional 11-2 victory.
"He wanted to play last night," Pritchett said of Dustin Blue. "As soon as we knew (of Matt's passing), the kids, the players and families wanted to play. We felt that was the best way to honor Matt. Matt would have wanted us to play. I think we showed it was the right decision."
Matt Blue was a three-sport athlete at Easton High before graduating in 2002. He went on to play goalkeeper for Salisbury University's soccer team before returning to teach in Talbot County. The former boys' head soccer coach at Easton High, he was diagnosed with cancer in December, 2022. Matt continued teaching at Easton Middle School, and remained an assistant on Easton's varsity baseball team until he passed Friday. Matt Blue was 40 years old.
"I thought the kids responded," Pritchett said. "They loved Matt Blue. They loved the coach. The community has a tremendous loss. It's going to be hard to replace him. I don't think we will.
"So I thought the kids, in the face of a lot of emotion, a lot of feelings, and a lot of loss, they did a good job," Pritchett continued. "They were here together playing the sport they love, supporting Dustin, the family. I'm very proud of them."
Matt Blue gave a speech prior to last year's St. Michaels at Easton game on April 13. Before Saturday's game, the public-address announcer reminded players, coaches and the large home crowd settled behind the backstop of one of Blue's main themes of recognizing the moment.
His son did just that on a wind-chilled afternoon of gray clouds and big patches of blue sky.
"It's incredible," Southern head coach Kyle Lynch said of Dustin. "The effort. Obviously the emotion. You don't know what's going through his head, but he threw tremendously. He was great. We have a lot respect for them and coach Pritchett. But what Dustin did was truly pretty special. Been around baseball for a long time and haven't seen anything like that."
Dustin's first pitch of the game was a strike to Thomas Martin. He got Martin on a grounder to short, then hit JC Wilson with a pitch. Easton catcher Colin Moody threw out Wilson trying to steal second then watched Dustin get a called strike three on Gavin Crandall to end the inning.
Easton's starting pitcher issued a one-out walk to Owen Meyers in the second, induced Andrew Cook into a fielder's choice, then zipped a pickoff throw to first that led to Cook getting caught in an inning-ending rundown.
Southern's Brendan Hinkle was hit by a pitch to lead off the third. But Nick Youmans grounded into a fielder's choice, struck out Dylan Clarke looking before Martin hit a deep fly that Warrior left fielder Carter Mooney made a nice play on.
Wilson lined Dustin's first offering of the fourth sharply through the middle for Southern's first hit. Wilson was erased on a fielder's choice. O'Brien was then hit by a pitch before Meyers dumped a singled into shallow left, loading the bases. Cook hit into a fielder's choice to plate the Bulldogs' first run before Pritchett came out to relieve Dustin with Garrett Fink.
"I thought he threw great," Pritchett said of Dustin (2-0), who remained in the game at shortstop. "I think (he threw) 60-something percent strikes. He commanded all three of his pitches. Again under a tremendous amount of pressure and emotion. Just showed a lot of character; lot of grit. It's a tremendous effort again in the face of tremendous loss and emotion. He's a tough kid. I'm proud of him."
Easton (3-1) scored all the runs it needed during a six-run second inning — all with two outs — against Bulldogs starter Crandall (1-1). Carter Mooney began the scoring, lining a stand-up RBI double down the left-field line. After Cullen Murphy walked, Dylan Cassell roped another run-producing double to left. Murphy scored on a wild pitch. Josh Dressler (2 for 4) singled to score Cassell for a 4-0 lead. Dressler eventually scored on a wild pitch before Dustin capped the scoring with an infield, RBI single.
The Warriors tacked on another five runs with two outs in the third for an 11-0 bulge. Murphy singled to center off reliever Rhett Dorval and was lifted for courtesy runner Mikey O'Connor. Cassell was hit by a pitch. Dressler singled into the hole at short, plating O'Connor. CJ Dugan (2 for 4) delivered the inning's big blow with a two-run single. Dustin (2 for 4) followed with an infield single.
Fink, who escaped a bases-loaded jam in the fourth, yielded a run in the fifth, but didn't give up a hit in two innings. He was relieved with two outs in the bottom of the sixth by O'Connor, who struck out three of the five batters he faced to close the win.
"I think it's a healthy distraction," Pritchett said of playing the game. "I think the kids needed it. They wanted it. And they proved it was a good decision for all of them. I thought their energy was high. They were positive despite the emotion."
After the game, Pritchett handed the game-ball to Dustin.
"Dustin looked fabulous," Pritchett said.
COLONEL 10, NORTH DORCHESTER 5
AMERICAN CORNER — Senior Daniel Hesson hurled a complete game Saturday morning, striking out nine, as the Colonels remained undefeated.
Derrick Mitchell hit a two-run homer for Colonel Richardson (5-0) and finished with three RBIs. Jordan Regulski and Johnny Beaven each had two hits.
SOFTBALL
NORTH DORCHESTER 7, COLONEL 2
AMERICAN CORNER — Emilee Cohee surrendered four hits, struck out 12 and issued one walk Saturday as the defending Class 1A state champions stayed unbeaten.
Cohee, Mackenzie Lewis, Maggie Hubbard and Maddie Nagel (two RBIs) each had two hits for the Eagles.
Makayla Newcomb suffered her first loss of the season as North Dorchester totaled 11 hits. Newcomb struck out six and walked two. Aubrey Taylor led Colonel with two hits, including a double.
QUEEN ANNE'S 8, CHESAPEAKE 5
CENTREVILLE — Abbie Denes blasted a three-run homer in the first inning and Autumn Huber was 3 for 4 with a four-inning homer Saturday to lead the Lions.
Caroline Taylor and Reece Brooks each had multiple-hit games for Queen Anne's. Hannah Martin earned the win, allowing just one run and four hits over six innings.
BOYS LACROSSE
EASTON 9, STEPHEN DECATUR 8
BERLIN — Drew Schmidt scored the game-winner in overtime Friday night as the Warriors edged the Seahawks in a rematch of last year's Bayside Conference championship.
Schmidt finished with a hat trick, Hudson Royer had four goals and an assist, and Tyler Rardin added two goals for Easton (1-1). Warrior goalie Jack Kilbourne made 11 saves.
GIRLS LACROSSE
NORTH CAROLINE 14, J.M. BENNETT 5
SALISBURY — Claire Blue scored four goals and Riley Walstrum had a hat trick to go with three assists Friday to pace the Bulldogs.
Reece Bisesi and Ashlynn Bisesi (assist) had two goals apiece for North Caroline. Calleigh Tribbett, Ashley Kercheval and Maddi Nicholson had one goal each.

title: Saints top Eagles, stay unbeaten
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Saints top Eagles, stay unbeaten

 April 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 879
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — St. Michaels High head baseball coach Brian Femi has always been known for the small things.And the small things again helped produce a victory Wednesday afternoon.
But the Saints also got a big pitching performance from Will Sherwood and a huge throw from center fielder Connor Wheeler that cut down a run at plate while helping St. Michaels remain unbeaten with a 4-1 victory over North Dorchester.
"Anytime you don't walk anybody you're going to be in a ballgame," Femi said. "Their pitcher (Wes Windsor) held us in check and we made a couple errors. And because Will pitched so well, it just kept us in a good position to win the game."
A junior right-hander, Sherwood (2-0) was touched for seven hits, but did not walk a batter and struck out 12 over six innings, mixing fastballs and curves.
"Coach was calling a lot of curveballs," Sherwood said of assistant Zach Wallace. "I was getting 'em over and they were swinging and missing at the ones that were low that he called. And locating the fastball was really nice today."
North Dorchester (4-2 overall, 0-1 North Bayside) took a 1-0 lead in the second inning. Nate Swann reached on an error to lead off the frame. Sherwood got a called strike three on Vernon Price, but Manny Reyes singled Swann to third, and Chance Blake singled down the left-field line to plate Swann. Sherwood ended the rally there, striking out the next two batters.
"He's picked up a little more velocity, but I've noticed he's got a lot more poise to him now," Femi said of Sherwood. "And I think it comes with experience. And he doesn't get rattled."
Sherwood could have gotten rattled in the fourth, when the Eagles' first two hitters got on. Instead, he struck out the next two batters before getting an inning-ending groundout.
The Saints (6-0, 1-0) took a 2-1 lead in the home fourth, but North Dorchester pieced together a two-out rally in the fifth, when Nate Fraccaroli reached on an error and Windsor dumped a single into center field. Swann followed by lacing a single up the middle that Wheeler got to quickly before unloading a strike to catcher Henry Mullikin, who tagged out Fraccaroli trying to score from second.
"I thought North Dorchester actually had the momentum in the early parts of the game until that throw," Femi said. "I think it just changed the whole complexion of it; took the wind out of their sails. And I think it gave us a little bit of an offensive boost once that happened.
"That ball was a little bit in the gap," Femi continued. "It wasn't like it was right to him. So he had to cut it off and then just made a throw right on the money. And that's a hard play for a catcher to make. People don't know. You got a guy barreling down on you. He still has to slide, but that's as bang bang as you can get."
Vernon Price hit a leadoff single in the sixth but Sherwood retired the next three batters to end his day. Anthony Massaro came on to pitch the seventh, allowing one hit.
"Pitchers did a great job today," North Dorchester head coach Dave Morrissette said. "Both sides. Will did a great job. Kept us off balance with that curveball a little bit, early especially. We hit some balls hard, but we got to score some guys once we get 'em on too."
St. Michaels struggled for offense, totaling six hits against Windsor, but scratched two runs across in the fourth inning.
Jacob Bealefeld worked a leadoff walk. Mullikin singled to right field. Pearson Greenwood's groundout to second moved Bealefeld to third. Pinch-hitter Eli Wallace then dropped a bunt to score Bealefield with the tying run.
Windsor hit Ethan Royer with a pitch. Royer stole second, broke for third and got caught in a rundown, allowing Mullikin to score from third for a 2-1 St. Michaels lead.
The Saints tacked on a run in the fifth. Hunter Gottleib reached on a bunt single and stole second. Wheeler hit a hard comebacker that Windsor made a nice play on before throwing to first for the out. Gottleib moved to third on the play and looked like he might get stranded, as Windsor retired Sherwood, then walked Bealefield. But Bealefeld broke for second, drawing a throw from Windsor. Gottleib raced home for a 3-1 lead.
"We bunt the ball and just try to put some balls in play," Femi said. "We had a lot of at-bats where we were striking out and just didn't put balls in play. He (Windsor) competes. I can't say enough about him and his catcher (TJ Leonard). We just had to do what we had to do not so much because of us, but because of them. I thought they played a really good game."
St. Michaels added a run in the sixth. Greenwood singled off the glove of the leaping Fraccaroli at second. Bobby Fink moved Greenwood to second with a sacrifice bunt. Two batters later, Gottleib popped up a bunt that Windsor made a lunging attempt to catch, but couldn't come up with the ball, allowing Greenwood to score from third.
Notes: Wheeler hit a two-out triple in the third but was stranded when Windsor got an inning-ending groundout.

title: Colonel strikes early, hangs on late
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonel strikes early, hangs on late

 April 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1096
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Perhaps one of the biggest reasons behind Daniel Hesson's success on the mound the past three seasons has been his practical approach."I felt like I had decent stuff," Colonel Richardson High's senior left-hander said. "Missed a couple locations. But you know, that's baseball. Sometimes you miss a spot, sometimes you put one where you want to put it. And other stuff happens. There's not much you can do about it."
Hesson tried to do as much as he could Thursday afternoon, limiting Easton to four runs over six-plus innings before the Warriors pieced together a late rally that fell short in an 11-8 loss to the Colonels.
"We got a saying: 'Winners find a way,'" Colonel first-year head coach Garrett Nepert said after his team's fourth straight win. "We found a way. It wasn't pretty, but winners find a way. So that's what we're kind of going with to make ourselves feel better today."
The Colonels (8-1 overall, 2-0 North Bayside) were feeling pretty good about themselves after sending 13 batters to the plate in a nine-run first inning that featured eight walks, Jordan Regulski's three-run double, and Hesson's RBI two-bagger.
Hesson (2-1) yielded three runs and six hits over 6 1/3 innings, striking out five and walking two. And though he surrendered Dustin Blue's leadoff homer to left-center field in the second inning, and Mikey O'Connor's two-out, two-run double in the fourth, he avoided the big inning for the most part.
"I was hitting locations early," Hesson said. "Missed a couple spots early. But really just movement on the changeup and everything like that was working well today."
O'Connor (0-1), Easton's starting pitcher, didn't get out of the first inning and was relieved by Pax Echternach. The Warriors' first reliever faced two men, including Regulski (2 for 3) who hit his bases-clearing double. Echternach was relieved by Cullen Murphy, who quieted the Colonels until the fourth, when Gavin Whitby (2 for 2) hit an RBI single and courtesy runner EJ Jones scored on a pop-out to first.
Down 11-3, Easton (4-4, 0-1), playing its fifth game in six days, had a potential rally going in the fifth, when Finn McGuckin and Dylan Cassell (2 for 3, RBI) led off with back-to-back singles. That rally was squelched though, when Josh Dressler hit a rope to short that Regulski lunged forward to catch. Colonel's shortstop, who has verbally committed to Wake Forest, got to his feet, stepped on second and threw to first to complete a triple play.
But Easton wasn't quite finished.
"We felt very comfortable today and that kind of came back and bit us," Hesson said. "They made it close in the very end. We got too comfortable. We have stuff to work on as a team. Me as well. This isn't our final form. We just got to get better as a team."
Hesson was relieved after allowing a one-out single to Carter Mooney in the home seventh. Reliever Jack Walls walked the first three batters he faced before Kayden Webb stung a two-run single to center, drawing Easton within 11-6. CJ Dugan's sacrifice fly trimmed Colonel's lead to 11-7. Blue walked before Colin Mooney singled to score Webb to make it 11-8. But Walls extinguished the rally there, getting a called third strike on O'Connor to end the game.
"At the end we didn't play our best baseball," Nepert said. "We have to continue to coach no matter what the lead is. Early on we kind of stuck to a good approach. Kind of went away from that later on in the game. But when you get a nine-run lead you get a little bit of a cushion which is a great thing."
Though his team's pitching was thin, Easton head coach Albert Pritchett liked how his team battled despite the early deficit.
"We probably had a few too many walks," said Pritchett, whose team issued 13. "But like the team we've always had in Easton, we never gave up. We had a hole. Cullen Murphy and Al Rhodes came in and held down things, and our offense chipped away. We got Hesson out of the game and got to the next pitcher and scored a few runs to make it competitive. Had a couple extra errors I would have liked to have got ridden of. But we're hitting the ball. I don't think this team thinks it's ever over."
ST. MICHAELS 16 KENT ISLAND 8
STEVENSVILLE — Jacob Bealefeld (2 for 2) homered, Connor Wheeler (2 for 4) doubled, and Will Sherwood (2 for 4) stole three bases as the Saints remained undefeated.
Anthony Massaro earned the win, allowing four runs (two earned) and eight hits over four innings. Brock Grow pitched three innings for the save.
Grow also went 2 for 2 with a pair of walks, and Bobby Fink has an two-run double for St. Michaels (7-0).
SOFTBALL
ST. MICHAELS 8 KENT ISLAND 7
STEVENSVILLE — Angel Bock picked up the win, allowing seven runs on 10 hits over seven innings Thursday to lead the Saints.
Bock, who struck out seven and walked just one, was 2 for 4 at the plate. Katie Jenkins also went 2 for 4 and Myla Ramey, Mercy Haddaway and Brianna Crow each had hits. Madi White drove in a pair of runs.
QUEEN ANNE'S 7 NORTH CAROLINE 6
CENTREVILLE — Autumn Huber drove in a pair of runs and Caroline Taylor went 3 for 4 Thursday as the Lions rallied from a five-run deficit to edge the Bulldogs.
Emily Hirschbock earned the win, allowing one hit and one run over 4 2/3 innings.
Queen Anne's scored five runs on four hits in the bottom of the third inning, with Mikayla Livingston and Emilie Smith hitting RBI singles.
BOYS LACROSSE
EASTON 16 CAMBRIDGE-SD 5
EASTON — Drew Schmidt and Tyler Rardin each had three goals and two assists Wednesday to lead the Warriors.
Campbell Taliaferro and Jackson Wieland had two goals and an assist apiece for Easton (2-1) and Charlie Kaminskas had a pair of goals. Hudson Royer and Sabin Long finished with one goal and one assist each, and Logan Friend and Luke Stanco netted one goal apiece. Easton's Angel Fernandez won five faceoffs and goalie Jack Kilbourne made three saves.
GIRLS LACROSSE
SSPP 24 SALISBURY SCHOOL 6
EASTON — Senior Morgan Quade totaled five goals and seven assists, and freshman Emery Zimmerman finished with four goals and three assists Wednesday as the Sabres improved to 5-1.
Caroline Ewing had four goals and one assist for Saints Peter and Paul, and Eryn Callahan (four assists), Kendall Kroniser (two assists), Avery McCall (assist) and Eden Zimmerman each had two goals. Emma Hainey, Samantha Murphy and Julia Spero added one goal apiece for the Sabres.

title: Seek, Saints outduel Palmer, Lions
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Seek, Saints outduel Palmer, Lions

 April 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1419
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Like many a game that shapes a division race, it was close.Each team turned an inning-ending double play.
Each team had a batter hit by a pitch and another intentionally walk.
Each team got outstanding performances from their big-name pitchers.
And each team finished with five hits.
But it was St. Michaels High's baseball team that produced the decisive — and what proved to be the last — hit. That hit came with two outs and the bases loaded in the bottom of the fifth inning Monday, when Jack Brennen chopped a slow bouncer down the third-base line for an infield hit that scored Pearson Greenwood with the winning run in a 3-2 Saints victory at Harold Baines Field.
St. Michaels (12-0 overall, 5-0 North Bayside) entered Tuesday tied atop the division with Colonel Richardson (12-1, 5-0) while Queen Anne's slipped to 9-3, 2-2.
"It was a very good high school baseball game," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said. "Both teams played well. It was an outstanding pitching duel. Both teams got timely hits. Both played good defense."
And both had scored two runs apiece heading into the bottom of the fifth.
That's when Will Sherwood lined a one-out single to center field. Queen Anne's right-hander Noah Palmer (3-1) walked Greenwood. Both runners advanced on a wild pitch before Palmer issued an intentional pass to Jacob Bealefeld, loading the bases. Henry Mullikin grounded to third baseman Jacob Clough, who threw home to force Sherwood at the plate for the second out.
Brennen then beat a grounder down the third-base line. Clough got to the ball, but didn't have time to make a throw to first as Greenwood raced home with the go-ahead run. Femi and Queen Anne's head coach Chris Fitzgerald agreed Brennen's bouncer was an infield hit — the last hit for either team the rest of the game.
"Heavyweight game for sure," Fitzgerald said. "They got the hit they needed and came away with the W."
Both pitchers were impressive, with St. Michaels senior left-hander Jacob Seek (4-0) striking out a season-high 13 in a complete-game victory. Seek allowed one earned run and walked two.
"This is what he's done all year," Femi said of Seek. "He just goes out and makes big pitches in big situations. The bigger the situation the bigger the pitcher. And he's a leader."
Queen Anne's Dalton Brown led off the game with a single, but Seek struck out the next three batters.
Down 2-0, the Lions had a rally working in the second, when Clough walked on four pitches and Colin Siwald singled to left. Seek fanned Bobby McCarthy, but Palmer reached with a bunt single up the third-base line, loading the bases. Gavin Leith grounded into a fielder's choice that plated Clough to make it 2-1. Seek ended the inning when Brown skied out to center.
"At moments it was little tight, but I think we did a good job of pulling out of it and being efficient," Seek said. "My curveball was on point today I felt like. I felt like I had a little mechanical issue that I had to (work the) kink out early. And I think when I figured that out in that second inning it kind of picked up for me and I was able to be more efficient with my pitches and hit my locations."
The Lions though pulled even in the top of the third. With one out, Seek struck out Dulin Clark. But the ball kicked away from Mullikin behind the plate. By the time St. Michaels' catcher located and retrieved the ball over by the St. Michaels dugout, Clark was on second. Evan Dickey then laced a 1-2 offering up the middle to score Clark with the tying run.
The closest Queen Anne's came to breaking the 2-2 tie was in the fourth. Leith reached on an infield hit and moved to second on a passed ball. After Brown was intentionally walk, Seek fanned Noah Cramer to end the inning.
Seek retired nine of the final 10 batters he faced. McCarthy reached with one out in the sixth when he was hit by a pitch before Palmer bounced to Bealefeld at third to a 5-4-3 inning-ending double play.
"That turned the game around I thought," Femi said. "Jake's played well for us all year. And that just swung the momentum our way."
Palmer delivered yet another quality performance for the Lions, striking out eight and walking four in 5 1/3 innings.
"I thought he was fantastic," Femi said of Palmer. "He beat us last year. We haven't hit him in two years. He competes. He changes speeds. He throws multiple pitches. I think he's one of the better pitchers in the Bayside."
But the Saints pushed two runs across in the home half of the first. Connor Wheeler was hit by a pitch and stole second base. Sherwood reached on an error, advancing Wheeler to third. Palmer looked like he might escape any damage when he struck out Greenwood and Bealefeld. But Mullikin drove a 1-1 pitch up the middle to score Wheeler and Sherwood for a 2-0 lead. Brennen followed with a single before Palmer fanned Bobby Fink to end the frame.
"After that first inning, it was rough," Palmer said. "But I came back and I feel like I was dialed in."
Blending his fastball and curve, Palmer wouldn't face more than four batters over the next three innings. Wheeler hit a two-out single in the second, stole second base and moved to third on a passed ball before Palmer got Sherwood to bounce out to third. The right-hander walked Bealefeld with one out in the third. Mullikin flew out to center fielder Brown, who fired a strike to first to double off Bealefield for the inning-ending double play.
Brock Grow got on via a two-out walk in the fourth and advanced to second on a passed ball. But Palmer got a called third strike on Ethan Royer to strand Grow. St. Michaels stranded seven baserunners, six in scoring position.
"He hasn't had a bad game," Fitzgerald said of Palmer. "We've put him up against all the big teams we got to go up against and we're proud the way he's handled himself all year. This wasn't surprising. Every game he's always performed like he did today. Just a stud for us. Proved it again today. Wish we could have gotten a couple more hits for him here and there and the game might have turned out different. But he did everything we asked of him today."
Palmer struck out Grow to open the sixth before reaching his pitch limit and being relieved by Brown, who struck out both batters he faced.
Queen Anne's stranded six, two in scoring position.

Townsend struck out five and walked three. Isabelle Ludwig drove in three runs for Easton and Olivia Orrell and Lyla Roe had multiple-hit games.
Avery Eaton had three RBIs for Kent Island. Hayven Applefeld, Bri Kurtz and Lizzie McConnell each had three hits for the Buccaneers.

EASTON — Emily Currie scored six goals Monday, and Miranda Stup and Dakota Lhotsky each had hat tricks as the Warriors posted their fifth win in six games.

title: Regulski, Hesson deliver Colonel to North championship
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Regulski, Hesson deliver Colonel to North championship

 April 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 746
 Words 

 Read News Document

 AMERICAN CORNER — Jordan Regulski never let the door get open. Daniel Hesson made sure it stayed shut.Colonel Richardson High's dynamic pitching duo combined to throw a two-hitter Tuesday as the Colonels defeated St. Michaels, 3-1, to clinch the North Bayside baseball championship.
"When you walk into a situation like this, I'm a lot more blessed than a lot of people that take over programs," Colonel Richardson first-year head coach Garrett Nepert said after the Colonels improved to 15-1 overall, 7-0 North Bayside with their 11th straight victory. "I'm grateful. But this is all about the kids. I don't do too much. They do it all."
Even if Colonels loses Thursday at North Dorchester, it would still win the division title based on defeating St. Michaels (14-2, 7-1). Colonel defeated the Saints, 6-5, last week, but Tuesday's second meeting between the two teams is the one that counts toward the division standings.
"We didn't deserve to win," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said. "You can't give a good team like this all the opportunities that we gave them. And they played better defense and made smarter plays that we did. I told our guys their baseball IQ just wasn't there today. I told them that's not their fault. That's my fault because we've got to find away to teach it better."
Regulski and St. Michaels ace Jacob Seek were locked in a scoreless duel, when Colonel scratched across two runs in the bottom of the fourth.
Brayden Dadds worked a one-out walk. Derrick Mitchell was hit by a pitch. Both runners advanced on a wild pitch. Manny Wallace then popped out to St. Michaels first baseman Anthony Massaro in foul territory on the first-base side. With no one covering home, Dadds broke for home and dove across the plate in a cloud of dust for a 1-0 lead. Massaro got the ball to catcher Hunter Gottleib, whose tried to throw out Mitchell at third. But the throw to third was off the mark, bringing home Mitchell for a 2-0 lead.
"We did what we needed to do for sure," Nepert said. "We still got a way to go. We've got a week before we've got to play our best baseball."
St. Michaels pulled within 2-1 in the top of the fifth. Regulski issued a leadoff walk to Ethan Royer. The junior right-hander struck out Brock Grow before getting Connor Wheeler to bounce into a fielder's choice. Wheeler stole second, moved to third on a passed ball, then raced home on a passed ball. Regulski struck out Jacob Bealefeld to end the inning.
Colonel regained its two-run lead in the home fifth. Seek walked Jack Walls and Regulski to open the inning. Hesson then dropped a bunt up the first-base line. Massaro fielded the ball, looked to third, then threw late to first, loading the bases. Seek fanned Dadds, but Walls scored on a passed ball to make it 3-1. Seek walked Mitchell before retiring the next two batters to end the inning.
Regulski yielded a clean single to Pearson Greenwood (2 for 3) to leadoff the second. But that was the only hit St. Michaels mustered against the Colonel starter. Regulski allowed one run, walked four, hit Will Sherwood twice with pitches and struck out seven.
"He competes," Femi said of Regulski, who has verbally committed to Wake Forest University. "He battles you. He is crazy athletic; makes plays that pitchers might not make, but makes them look easy."
Hesson came on at the start of the sixth inning. The senior left-hander who is headed to Salisbury University after graduation, gave up a one-out single to Greenwood in the sixth and nothing else, striking out four of the seven batters he faced.
"They're both fantastic kids," Femi said of Hesson and Regulski, who have worked at Femi's baseball camps the past two summers. "Not only are they good baseball players but they're good people.
"He carries this team," Femi said of Hesson. "Mentally, he's a leader for them."
Nepert kept his praise for his two pitchers brief and to the point.
"Excellent," Nepert said. "That's about all I got. I thought they attacked the zone. They worked to their strengths."
Seek, who struck out seven and walked seven, gave up a leadoff single to Walls (2 for 3) to start the game. It was Colonel's only hit off Seek. Grow came on in relief with a man on in the sixth. he gave up a one-out single to Walls in the sixth and finished with two strikeouts and a walk.

title: Decatur has Wright stuff, tops Colonels
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Decatur has Wright stuff, tops Colonels

 May 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1085
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — He lost his no-hit bid with two outs in the sixth inning.Two batters later, he lost his shot for a shutout.
But Stephen Decatur High senior Matt Wright had been dominant for too long, and his offense had given him a lead that proved too much to overcome Wednesday night, as the Seahawks defeated Colonel Richardson, 13-4, for their second Bayside Conference championship in three years at Arthur W. Perdue Stadium.
"He threw really well," Colonel Richardson head coach Garrett Nepert said of Wright, who is headed to Division II Mars Hill (North Carolina) University. "Commanded the zone. Threw multiple pitches. He did excellent."
As did Colonel Richardson starting pitcher Daniel Hesson. The senior left-hander bound for Salisbury University gave up A.J. Kolb's leadoff double in the first inning and little else until Ryder Swanson's double to leadoff the fourth ended his day on the mound.
"He did excellent," Nepert said of Hesson, who gave up one run and two hits, struck out five, walked three and hit one batter.
After yielding Kolb's leadoff double in the first, Hesson recorded back-to-back strikeouts then walked Nate Brozonski. Kolb stole third base but was stranded, as Hesson induced Swanson's inning-ending fly-out.
Hesson worked out of another jam in the second. After issuing consecutive one-out walks to Johnny Hobgood and Eric Braica, Hesson got a called third strike on Caden Shockley. Both runners advanced on a passed ball during Shockley's at-bat, but again Hesson kept the Seahawks (17-2) off the board, getting Kolb to ground out to third to end the inning.
Hesson's easiest inning was the third. Waylon Hobgood was hit by a pitch to lead off the frame, but was thrown out trying to steal second by catcher Cameron Todd. Lukas Loring then hit a sinking line drive that Colonel right fielder Derrick Mitchell made a nice diving catch on for the second out. Hesson fanned Brozonski to end the inning, then gave up Swanson's leadoff double in the fourth, bringing on reliever Jack Walls. Hesson took over at first base.
"We can't go into Saturday without our ace," said Nepert, whose 17-2 team is scheduled to host either Cambridge-South Dorchester or Kent County on Saturday in a Class 1A East Region I semifinal. "This is important. Obviously a lot of people here. Lot of pride in this game. But at the end of the day, you know, this weekend, on forward."
Jackson Cheung moved Swanson to third with a sacrifice bunt. Walls walked Johnny Hobgood, then tried picking off Hobgood at first. Swanson broke for home, Hesson's throw from first, for a 1-0 Decatur lead.
Decatur busted the game open in the top of the fifth, scoring eight runs on five hits. Walls surrendered a two-run single to Lukas Loring and a two-run double to Swanson, giving the Seahawks a 5-0 lead.
Kenton Robbins took over for Walls. Decatur extended its lead to 7-0 against the right-hander, who after four batters was relieved by Jordan Regulski. Colonel's junior right-hander got Kolb to bounce into a 1-2-3 double play for the inning's first outs, then yielded Waylon Hobgood's two-run single to right for a 9-0 Decatur lead.
"We've had some struggles laying off pitches a little bit high in the zone," Decatur head coach Rich Ferro said. "And we're not high-ball hitters. We have to live down. We finally did that and then went with the ball the other way.
"And then we took bags," Ferro said of his team's five stolen bases. "We were trying to time him out on the mound and we got runners in motion. And we bunted successfully. We played pretty good baseball today."
The Seahawks also got a pretty outstanding performance from Wright (4-0).
The left-hander, who walked two, carried a no-hitter into the sixth, when he notched his seventh and eighth strikeouts to start the inning. Regulski then hit a rocket off Cheung at third base that was ruled a hit. Though some in the crowd disagreed with the ruling, Hesson followed with a single to left. Brayden Dadds then hit a comebacker to the mound. Wright bobbled the ball briefly then made a low throw to first that first baseman Brozonski couldn't dig out. Regulski scored on the play, making it 9-1, and bringing on reliever Caleb Loring.
"He was really, really good. That's the best way to put it," Ferro said of Wright. "When he's able to command the zone and expand a little bit with is two-seam (fastball), it makes it really difficult on right-hand batters because it takes off like crazy.
"Matt was lights out," Ferro added. "It took us a couple innings to get going. He kept us in the ballgame and that was the biggest thing. He gave us a shot to be competitive today. And then the offense came alive and he settled back in. Had a little hiccup in the fifth. We wanted to extend him to about 80, 85 (pitches) and that's about where he ended up."
Manny Wallace greeted Caleb Loring with a single to center that scored courtesy runner Preston Rickwood. Caleb Rouser singled into shallow right field, plating Dadds to make it 9-3. Gavin Whitby then hit a bad-hop single that scored Wallace, trimming the Decatur lead to five. But Caleb Loring got Mitchell to bounce out to end the inning.
"We put up a fight," Nepert said. "I would have liked to have seen it a little bit earlier in the game. I thought we were kind of flat. But if we're going to have that, today's the day and not Saturday."
Decatur tacked on four more runs in the top of the seventh. Brozonski hit a two-run single, Swanson lined an RBI double to left, and Cheung produced a run-scoring groundout.
Swanson finished 3 for 4 with three RBIs for Decatur. Waylon Hobgood (2 for 3) Lukas Loring (1 for 5) and Brozonski (1 for 3) each drove in two runs. Kolb also had two hits for the Seahawks, who finished with 10. Colonel had five hits.
SOFTBALLMARDELA 4, NORTH DORCHESTER 0SALISBURY — Hayden Adkins and Ava Twilley combined for a two-hit shutout Wednesday, as the Warriors blanked the Eagles at Salisbury University for their second straight Bayside Conference championship.
Adkins yielded two hits over four innings, striking out four and walking two. Twilley, who recorded her 300th career strikeout, pitched three scoreless innings, fanning five and walking one.
Twilley was 2 for 4 with two RBIs, Lexie Guy was 2 for 4 with an RBI, and Camryn Dorr was 2 for 4 for Mardela.
Emilee Cohee and Maddie Nagel each had one hit for North Dorchester.

title: Echternach, Fink, Murphy team to no-hit Wi-Hi as Warriors advance
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Echternach, Fink, Murphy team to no-hit Wi-Hi as Warriors advance

 May 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 663
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — His pitching staff plagued by injury since the beginning of the season, Easton High head baseball coach Albert Pritchett decided to take the committee approach heading into the postseason.That plan worked beautifully Thursday, as Pax Echternach, Dylan Fink and Cullen Murphy combined to throw a no-hitter, leading the Warriors to a 13-0 five-inning victory over Wicomico in a Class 2A East Region II quarterfinal on a day when its ball field was renamed Warrior Field in memory of former assistant coach Matt Blue.
A longtime Talbot County teacher and coach, Blue died on April 5, 2024 after a 17-month battle with cancer.
"I think it was perfect," Pritchett said of the field's renaming, which was celebrated with a brief ceremony prior the game before the field's updated scoreboard with Blue's name across the bottom was unveiled. "It was done as a community effort from his fellows teachers from the middle school, other Talbot County school teachers and community members. I think the Talbot County School teachers and community really stepped. They raised the money, got it approved, and I felt it was perfect. I just kind of shows you what kind of an impact he had."
Third-seeded Easton (9-9) advances to the 2A East Region II semifinals and will play at No. 2 seed and defending 2A state champion Parkside (13-4) on Saturday at 11 a.m.
Wicomico finished the season 1-17.
Echternach, who had only started on the mound once before this season, got the news he was the Warrior starter not long after he and his teammates showed up at the field.
"I didn't know I was (starting). But when he (Pritchett) said it I was kind of happy," Echternach said.
Pritchett may have been the happiest of Warriors as he watched his sophomore right-hander pitched 3 1/3 innings on no-hit ball, striking out two and walking just one.
"We're very proud of Pax," Pritchett said. "Stepped up against (James M.) Bennett (near the end of the regular season). Stepped up against Wi-Hi. Threw strikes. He mixed up his pitches well. Had a lot of first-pitch outs. Got them swinging, which is the key."
Echternach admitted he was a little nervous early, "when I was trying to figure out my pitches. After the first few pitches I was fine. I was confident in what I was doing.
"Probably my fastball the most," Echternach said when asked what was working. "It was the only thing I could really locate. And my changeup as well."
After issuing a one-out walk to Kayden Fryling, Echternach was relieved by Fink. Warrior catcher Colin Mooney threw out Fryling trying to steal second for the inning's second out. Fink walked Ayden George but then fanned Matthew Bier to end the fourth.
Murphy retired the side in order in the fifth.
The Warriors took advantage of three errors and a hit batsman to build a 3-0 lead in the bottom of the second.
Designated hitter Kayden Webb then triggered a four-run third by launching a Noah Riggin delivery over the left-field fence for a leadoff homer. CJ Dugan doubled to right and was moved to third on Colin Mooney's bunt single. Dugan then raced home, when Colin Mooney (2 for 3) drew a throw to second on a steal attempt, making it 5-0 Easton.
The Warriors added two more runs before the third was complete, then stretched their lead to 13 in the home fourth. Chris Jones relieved Riggin after two batters. Easton scored on an error, another throw down to second, and Mike O'Connor's run-producing groundout.
Carter Mooney doubled. After Jonah Rich was hit by a pitch, Al Rhodes' single to left was misplayed into a two-base error, plating two more runs. Dylan Cassell's single scored Rhodes with the game's last run.
"I feel confident we can hit the ball against most teams," Pritchett said. "And we can manufacture runs. Our defense has been strong throughout the year. We got to throw strikes, keep the pace moving. When we throw strikes, we're in every ballgame. When we don't throw strikes it's trouble."
